public_rationale: The original RLI report, submitted on October 30, 2025, reports a 2.5% automation rate for its highest-performing tested agent on real-world projects evaluated for end-to-end performance [e1]. This supports the numerical claim within that benchmark's scope [e1].
limitations: The benchmark result does not establish the share of all occupations AI can perform or aggregate economic value from LLM use [e1].
Support is limited to the original evaluation and its tested agents [e1].
The supplied evidence does not verify the Washington Post's wording or attribution.

statement.excerpt: Update: This is consistent with the finding of the Remote Labor Index that AI could only do about 2.5% of jobs, reported recently by the Washington Post.
statement.document_title: Let’s be honest, Generative AI isn’t going all that well

from_speaker: finding of the Remote Labor Index
AI could only do about 2.5% of jobs
reported recently by the Washington Post
our_interpretation: Because the sentence expressly attributes a finding to RLI, jobs means the commissioned projects in that benchmark.
The percentage refers to the best tested agent's end-to-end completion rate, not every agent's rate or the share of all occupations that AI can perform.
The target is the original RLI evaluation reported in 2025, rather than benchmark updates after the post.
Consistent with is read as compatibility with limited autonomous performance, not proof of small aggregate economic benefits.
The Washington Post attribution is checked separately from the primary numerical finding.
criteria.support_condition: The original RLI report records approximately 2.5% as the highest end-to-end project completion rate among evaluated agents.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The original report gives a materially different leading completion rate, or the 2.5% figure measures something other than successful completion of benchmark projects.
